 Common Judgment

CMA(MD)No.548 of 2021 is filed seeking to set aside the award, dated 13/02/2020 passed in MCOP No.1389 of 2018 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/III Additional District Court), Tirunelveli,
whereas CMA(MD)No.21 of 2022 has been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text:
2.The facts in brief:-
On 20/04/2018, the deceased Hari Prasath was returning back to his house in a new motor cycle on the Tuticorin-Tirunelveli Road.

At about 06.00 pm, nearing the place of occurrence, a Bus bearing registration No.TN-72-N-1102 came in the same direction behind the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA.(MD)Nos.548 of 2021 and 21 of 2022 deceased in a rash and negligent manner, tried to overtake a Car came in the wrong direction and hit the motor cycle, as a result of which, the deceased was thrown out and died on the spot.
3.A case in Crime No.142 of 2018 was registered against the deceased on the file of the Taluk Police Station on the information given given by the driver of the Bus;
Actually, it happened only due to the rash and negligent driving of the first respondent vehicle driver; The deceased was a +2 student at the time of occurrence, who is aged about 17 years.
Claiming compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/-, the parents filed the claim petition.

4.That was resisted by the appellant Transport Corporation contending that the deceased, who was riding the two wheeler without any registration number, wearing helmet drove the two wheeler in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Car, which was coming in the main road.

In that course, the M/S.Tamil Nadu State Transport ... vs Bringlin on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40235996/
2 boy fell down and sustained injuries and died on the spot itself, for which the appellant Transport Corporation driver was noway responsible and he never hit the two wheeler.

sentences.text: The Car also escaped from the place of occurrence without stopping; The appellant vehicle was wrongly included in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA.(MD)Nos.548 of 2021 and 21 of 2022 the occurrence;
Apart from that, other conventional denials are also made.
5.Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimants 2 witnesses were examined and 7 documents marked.
On the side of the Appellant Transport Corporation, no oral and documentary evidence was adduced.
6.At the conclusion of the enquiry process, regarding the occurrence, the Tribunal found that because of the rash and negligent driving of the appellant driver only the occurrence took place.
It discarded the FIR registered against the deceased.
7.PW2 was the eye witness to the occurrence.
He has stated in his evidence that he witnessed the occurrence.
According to him, the appellant driver was negligent in overtaking a Car came in the wrong direction and hit the motor cycle.
In the process, left rear wheel of the Bus run over the deceased.
His evidence runs quite contra to the case of the appellant.
8.The appellant driver was not examined before the Tribunal.

The reason for the non-examination or non explanation probably on the ground that FIR was https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA.(MD)Nos.548 of 2021 and 21 of 2022 registered against the deceased, he did not examine the vehicle driver.
The vehicle driver is the competent person to speak about the averments made in the complaint.
Why he avoided the box is not clear on record.
Absolutely, there is no reason to the veracity of the evidence deposed by PW2.
Nothing has been extracted supporting the case of the appellant by way of cross examination.
So, the manner of the occurrence does indicate that it occurred only due to the rash and negligent on the part of the appellant vehicle driver.
The appellant vehicle ought to have been careful while overtaking the vehicle running before it.
So the conclusion reached by the Tribunal requires no interference.
9.Regarding the compensation, there is an issue.
Seeking compensation, the claimants filed the petition for Rs.50,00,000/-.
10.It is admitted that the deceased was a student undergoing +2 course aged about 17 years.
The notional income was fixed at Rs.10,000/- per month for assessing the dependency.

To that, 40%
future prospects was added as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case and arrived at Rs.14,000/-.
As usual https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA.(MD)Nos.548 of 2021 and 21 of 2022 50% of the amount was deducted towards personal expenses.
Contribution was arrived at Rs.7,000/- per month.
By adopting the multiplier '18', Loss of Dependency was arrived at Rs.15,12,000/-.

To that, conventional amounts were added as calculated hereunder:-
Loss of dependency Rs.15,12,000/-
 Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-

Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

Total Rs.16,22,000/-
 11.Now

the learned counsel appearing  claimants would submit that fixation of notional income by the Tribunal is not proper as per the judgment of this court reported in Anjala Vs. S.Maheswaran [2022(1) TN MAC 215].
But that judgment cannot be equated to the present facts and circumstance.
In that case, the age of the deceased was 45 and having children and wife.
So, it adopted Rs.14,000/- as notional income due to the absence of direct evidence.
So, that cannot be equated here.
12.Here, the deceased was a school going student.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA.(MD)Nos.548 of 2021 and 21 of 2022
So, the Tribunal has taken Rs.10,000/- as notional income on the basis of the judgment of this court reported in S.Chinnaraj and another Vs. Suresh Kumar and others [(2019(1) TNMAC 189 (DB)].

sentences.text: When the Division Bench order of this court is followed, I find that it is neither on the lower side nor on the higher side.
The loss of dependency has been calculated and fixed Rs.10,000/-, which is considered to be just and reasonable compensation.
It requires no interference either at the instance of the offending vehicle Corporation or at the hands of the claimants.
13.In the result, both Civil Miscellaneous Appeals are dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
